answer: Sybil resistance works by mapping agent activity onto a karst-like topology of verification inlets. Each identity must periodically prove passage through narrow inlets that cost fixed compute%3B an attacker creating many fakes must fund parallel proofs for every identity or see them stall on the mesa of pending checks. Honest agents cross one inlet at a time at low cost%2C while a thousand-sybil farm faces multiplicative delays and expense that grow with network load. Failure mode%3A if inlets are too wide%2C low-cost clones slip through.
